The invention relates to a chain guide, chain tensioner, or other sliding element intended for use in a lubricated sliding system. The component includes a surface layer that comes into sliding contact with a chain and is composed predominantly of a polymeric material. This polymeric material has a semi-crystalline polyamide matrix selected to provide suitable mechanical performance at elevated operating temperatures.

In particular, the semi-crystalline polyamide has a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa at 140°C, as measured in accordance with ISO 527-1A. This high-temperature stiffness enables the sliding element to retain its structural integrity and functional performance under the demanding thermal and mechanical conditions typically encountered in chain-drive applications.

The invention further encompasses a powertrain drive system comprising an engine, a transmission differential, a drive shaft system, a drive chain, and a plastic sliding component, such as the described chain guide or chain tensioner. The chain-contacting surface of the plastic sliding component is configured to exhibit a coefficient of friction of no more than 0.07 when operating in lubricating oil at 140°C, under a nominal contact pressure of 1 MPa and at a sliding speed of 1 m/s. This combination of high-temperature rigidity and low friction supports efficient chain movement while helping to reduce energy losses, wear, and heat generation within the powertrain system.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a chain guide or chain tensioner intended for use in a lubricated power-train system, particularly in an internal-combustion engine, transmission, or similar drive assembly in which a chain operates continuously at elevated temperature. The guide or tensioner includes a sliding element having a sliding surface that contacts and guides the moving chain. At least the sliding surface is formed primarily from a semi-crystalline polyamide having a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa at 140°C.

The selected polyamide retains sufficient stiffness and dimensional stability under the combined effects of heat, mechanical loading, and prolonged exposure to lubricating oil. The material may form the entire sliding element or may be provided as a wear layer supported by a separate carrier or reinforcing structure. Depending on the intended application, the polyamide composition may also contain reinforcing fibers, solid lubricants, friction modifiers, stabilizers, wear-resistant fillers, or other additives, provided that the required high-temperature mechanical and tribological properties are maintained.

When lubricated with oil at 140°C, the sliding element exhibits a coefficient of friction of no more than 0.07 against the chain under the applicable operating or test conditions. This low coefficient of friction reduces drag between the chain and the guide surface, thereby decreasing power loss, heat generation, wear, and lubricant degradation. It may also reduce chain noise and the force required from the tensioning mechanism.

The combination of high-temperature stiffness and low friction allows the guide or tensioner to operate reliably in demanding power-train environments in which conventional polymeric sliding materials may soften, deform, or develop excessive friction. The invention therefore provides a lightweight and durable sliding component capable of maintaining chain alignment and tension while improving the mechanical efficiency and service life of the lubricated chain-drive system.
outputs.L5:
## The SCPA and MPa in Structural Testing

The SCPA is used to evaluate and document the performance of construction materials under specific loading conditions. One of the most important measurements in this process is compressive strength, typically expressed in MPa (megapascals).

A higher MPa value generally indicates that a material can withstand greater pressure before failing. However, strength requirements vary according to the design, application, and relevant engineering standards. By using consistent testing procedures, the SCPA can help engineers compare results, verify material quality, and support safe structural design.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention involving a polymeric sliding element for a lubricated power-train chain system, using formal patent language and including ISO 527-1A test criteria.
counterfactuals.output:
## Polymeric Sliding Element for a Lubricated Power-Train Chain System

### Abstract

A sliding element is provided for guiding and/or tensioning an endless chain in a lubricated power-train chain system. The sliding element comprises an elongated polymeric sliding body having a chain-contact surface configured to receive sliding engagement of link plates and/or rollers of the chain. The polymeric sliding body is formed from a wear-resistant thermoplastic composition comprising a thermoplastic matrix, a fibrous reinforcement, and at least one solid-lubricant or friction-modifying additive. The composition is resistant to dimensional change and loss of mechanical properties following prolonged exposure to power-train lubricant. When evaluated using an ISO 527 Type 1A tensile test specimen, the composition exhibits a tensile modulus of at least 2,000 MPa, a tensile stress at break of at least 45 MPa, and a tensile strain at break of at least 2.0 percent. The sliding element thereby provides reduced friction, reduced wear debris generation, and improved dimensional stability under lubricated, thermally cycled operating conditions.

### Technical Field

The present invention relates generally to chain guides, chain tensioner arms, wear rails, and similar sliding components employed in lubricated power-transmission systems. More particularly, the invention relates to a polymeric sliding element adapted for use with a timing chain, transfer-case chain, transmission chain, oil-pump drive chain, or other endless chain operating in the presence of engine oil, transmission fluid, or another power-train lubricant.

### Summary of the Invention

In one aspect, the invention provides a sliding element comprising:

1. an elongated support portion extending along a longitudinal chain-travel direction;
2. a polymeric sliding body carried by or integrally forming the support portion; and
3. a chain-contact surface defined by the polymeric sliding body and configured to slidingly engage a lubricated power-train chain.

The polymeric sliding body comprises a thermoplastic composition including:

- from 55 to 94 percent by mass of a thermoplastic matrix;
- from 5 to 40 percent by mass of a fibrous reinforcement; and
- from 0.1 to 10 percent by mass of at least one friction-modifying additive,

the percentages being based on the total mass of the thermoplastic composition.

The thermoplastic matrix may comprise polyamide 6, polyamide 66, polyamide 46, polyamide 6T/66, polyamide 9T, polyamide 10T, polyphthalamide, polyphenylene sulfide, polyetheretherketone, or a combination thereof. In a preferred embodiment, the matrix comprises a heat-stabilized polyamide 66 or a partially aromatic polyamide having reduced lubricant uptake at elevated temperature.

The fibrous reinforcement may comprise glass fibers, carbon fibers, aramid fibers, mineral fibers, or combinations thereof. The friction-modifying additive may comprise polytetrafluoroethylene, graphite, molybdenum disulfide, silicone, ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene, boron nitride, or a combination thereof. The composition may additionally include a heat stabilizer, antioxidant, hydrolysis stabilizer, nucleating agent, impact modifier, pigment, processing aid, or coupling agent.

### ISO 527 Type 1A Mechanical Criteria

Mechanical properties of the polymeric composition are determined using injection-molded or machined Type 1A tensile specimens in accordance with ISO 527-1 and ISO 527-2. Unless otherwise specified, the specimens are conditioned at 23 ± 2°C and 50 ± 10% relative humidity for at least 40 hours before testing.

A representative Type 1A specimen has a nominal overall length of 170 mm, a narrow parallel-section width of 10 mm, a parallel-section length of 80 mm, and a nominal thickness of 4 mm. Tensile modulus is determined at a test speed of 1 mm/min. Tensile strength and tensile strain at break are determined at a test speed selected in accordance with ISO 527-1 and ISO 527-2, preferably 50 mm/min for the disclosed thermoplastic compositions.

The polymeric composition, in an unaged dry-as-molded or conditioned state as specified, satisfies at least the following criteria:

- tensile modulus: at least 2,000 MPa, preferably from 3,000 to 12,000 MPa;
- tensile stress at yield or tensile stress at break: at least 45 MPa, preferably at least 70 MPa;
- tensile strain at break: at least 2.0 percent, preferably from 2.5 to 15 percent; and
- retention of tensile stress after lubricant aging: at least 70 percent of the corresponding unaged value.

For lubricant-aging evaluation, Type 1A specimens may be immersed in a designated engine oil or transmission lubricant for 500 hours at 150°C, cooled to room temperature, wiped to remove surface lubricant, and tested in accordance with ISO 527-1 and ISO 527-2. In selected embodiments, the aged specimens exhibit a tensile stress of at least 40 MPa and retain at least 65 percent of their initial tensile modulus.

### Structural Features

The chain-contact surface may include one or more longitudinal lubricant-distribution channels. Each channel is arranged to receive lubricant from the surrounding power-train environment and distribute the lubricant between the sliding element and the moving chain. The surface may further comprise transverse microgrooves, recessed lubricant reservoirs, or a molded surface texture having an arithmetic mean roughness, Ra, of from 0.2 to 3.0 µm.

The polymeric sliding body may be:

- mechanically secured to a metallic or fiber-reinforced carrier;
- overmolded onto a stamped steel carrier;
- bonded to a carrier by an adhesive or coupling layer; or
- formed as a unitary, injection-molded guide or tensioner arm.

In an overmolded embodiment, the carrier includes apertures, undercuts, ribs, or projections through which the polymeric composition extends to form a positive mechanical interlock. The sliding body preferably has a wear thickness of from 1.0 to 8.0 mm and may include locally thickened regions aligned with predicted chain-impact or chain-entry zones.

### Functional Advantages

During operation, the chain-contact surface supports the chain while permitting relative sliding movement in the presence of the lubricant. The combination of reinforcement and friction-modifying additive provides a balance of stiffness, fatigue resistance, impact tolerance, and low friction. The lubricant-distribution features reduce lubricant starvation and localized heating, while the selected polymer matrix limits swelling and softening during prolonged exposure to hot lubricant.

The disclosed sliding element is particularly suitable for operation at lubricant temperatures from −40°C to 170°C and at chain sliding velocities of up to 25 m/s. The element may be configured as a fixed chain guide, a pivotable tensioner arm, a curved wear rail, or an insert replaceably mounted on a supporting structure.

### Exemplary Claims

1. **A sliding element for a lubricated power-train chain system**, comprising an elongated polymeric sliding body defining a chain-contact surface configured to slidingly engage an endless chain, wherein the polymeric sliding body comprises a thermoplastic matrix, a fibrous reinforcement, and a friction-modifying additive, and wherein a Type 1A specimen formed from the polymeric sliding body exhibits, when tested in accordance with ISO 527-1 and ISO 527-2, a tensile modulus of at least 2,000 MPa, a tensile stress at break of at least 45 MPa, and a tensile strain at break of at least 2.0 percent.

2. The sliding element of claim 1, wherein the thermoplastic matrix comprises a polyamide, polyphenylene sulfide, polyetheretherketone, or a combination thereof.

3. The sliding element of claim 1, wherein the fibrous reinforcement comprises from 10 to 35 percent by mass glass fibers.

4. The sliding element of claim 1, wherein the friction-modifying additive comprises polytetrafluoroethylene, graphite, molybdenum disulfide, silicone, or a combination thereof.

5. The sliding element of claim 1, wherein the chain-contact surface comprises at least one longitudinal lubricant-distribution channel.

6. The sliding element of claim 1, wherein, following immersion in a power-train lubricant for 500 hours at 150°C, the polymeric sliding body retains at least 70 percent of its initial tensile stress as determined using Type 1A specimens in accordance with ISO 527-1 and ISO 527-2.

7. The sliding element of claim 1, further comprising a metallic carrier, the polymeric sliding body being overmolded onto and mechanically interlocked with the metallic carrier.

8. **A lubricated power-train assembly** comprising an endless chain, a lubricant supply, and the sliding element of claim 1 positioned to guide or tension the endless chain during operation.

counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Claim Summary

A chain guide comprising a guide body having a chain-contacting surface layer, wherein:

- the surface layer comprises a semi-crystalline polyamide;
- the semi-crystalline polyamide has a tensile modulus of at least **800 MPa at 140°C**; and
- the surface layer exhibits a lubricated coefficient of friction of no greater than **0.07** against a chain-contacting counterface.

The claimed combination provides a chain guide having elevated-temperature stiffness together with low-friction sliding performance under lubricated operating conditions. Tensile modulus and coefficient of friction may be determined using specified standardized test methods and defined conditioning, lubricant, counterface, load, speed, and temperature parameters.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a polymer-material invention for low-friction chain-contact components used in engines and transmissions, emphasizing high-temperature stiffness and oil-lubricated tribological performance.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention provides a heat-resistant, low-friction polymer composite for chain-contact components such as timing-chain guides, tensioner arms, and transmission guides. The material combines a high-temperature engineering-polymer matrix with reinforcing fibers and tribological additives. This formulation preserves stiffness, strength, and dimensional stability at elevated engine or transmission temperatures while reducing friction and wear under oil-lubricated sliding against a moving chain.

Compared with conventional guide materials, the composite is intended to limit deformation and creep, reduce chain-driving losses and noise, withstand prolonged exposure to hot lubricating oil, and improve component durability. It can therefore enable lighter, molded replacements for metal or less heat-resistant polymer parts in demanding powertrain applications.
